overview: This State Department file gathers biographical intelligence and diplomatic correspondence concerning prominent Japanese military, political, naval, and aristocratic figures, principally during the tense prewar years of the 1930s and 1940. It includes military-attaché profiles of Issaku Nishihara, Hideki Tojo, and Yoshitsugu Tatekawa; personal exchanges concerning the illness of the pro-American statesman Count Kentaro Kaneko; and extensive records of American responses to the deaths, funerals, and memorialization of Prince Kinmochi Saionji, Admiral Heihachiro Togo, and Prince Iesato Tokugawa. Much of the file documents the careful negotiation of condolences, presidential representation, naval participation, publicity, ceremonial precedence, and Japanese acknowledgments, alongside press coverage and controversy over NBC’s unsuitable music during Togo’s funeral observances.
interest: Shows how ceremonial gestures like condolences, flag lowering and special representatives worked as substantive diplomacy, and the NBC incident.
